newsitem.title: USA: Heir sells 9 million shares for $720 million.
newsitem.headline: Heir sells 9 million shares for $720 million.

text.p: John Dorrance III, the grandson of the founder of Campbell Soup Co., sold 9 million shares of Campbell stock for $720 million Thursday in one of the largest single trades ever on the New York Stock Exchange.

Dorrance has been selling blocks of Campbell stock in recent months in an apparent bid to cash in on the strength of the shares. The selling has accelerated since Campbell announced a major restructuring and stock buyback programme on Sept. 5, which has given an added boost to the share price.

Campbell said it was not involved in the trade, which crossed at $80 a share on the New York Stock Exchange at 12:32 p.m. EST. The Camden, N.J.-based soup and food company later confirmed that the shares sold had been owned by Dorrance, the grandson of Campbell founder Dr. John Dorrance.
J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc. handled the transaction and probably lined up the buyer or buyers, Wall Street sources said.
The trade, equal to almost 4 percent of Campbell's 247 million shares outstanding, was not part of the share buyback plan, a Campbell spokesman said.
The NYSE said the trade was the seventh biggest block trade in dollar terms ever on the exchange, and the largest in 3-1/2 years.
